A man in his 70s with no history of chronic or allergic rhinosinusitis presented to the emergency department with a headache for 2 weeks and vision loss in the right eye for 2 days. Three weeks prior, he had rhinorrhea and was diagnosed with COVID-19. He recovered from COVID-19 but developed a worsening right-sided headache 1 week later and right vision loss 2 days prior to presentation.

Right eye visual acuity was limited to hand-motion detection, with severe pain on ocular motion.

clinical_record:
A 46-year-old woman presented with recurrent, intermittent, painless hematuria over the past six years. Two years ago she was diagnosed with systemic hypertension and has been taking irbesartan 150 mg daily, along with various herbal remedies for her hematuria. 

On examination, her vital signs were within normal limits, and systemic examination was unremarkable. Urinalysis showed 3+ blood and 5.1 red blood cells per high-power field; phase-contrast microscopy revealed 70% dysmorphic red cells. Serum electrolytes and renal function tests were normal. An abdominal ultrasonogram demonstrated a fatty liver and multiple small (“sand-like”) stones in the left kidney. 

To further evaluate her hematuria, a contrast-enhanced CT scan of the abdomen was performed.

clinical_record:
A 5-month-old dark-skinned boy was seen for evaluation of a congenital skin lesion on the left supraclavicular area. At birth, the lesion measured 11 cm × 3.5 cm; at 5 months it measured 10 cm × 2.5 cm. On examination, it was a single, nonpulsatile, well-demarcated, dark brown atrophic plaque with a linear midline depression and an elevated, compressible, soft border that was paler than the central portion. Birth and neonatal history were unremarkable; the patient was healthy and not on medications. The initial differential diagnosis included smooth muscle hamartoma, semiannular lipoatrophy, and, less likely, a rapidly involuting congenital hemangioma (RICH). A small vein (~0.3 mm) was visible to the naked eye within the plaque. To avoid puncturing larger vessels during a planned biopsy, an AccuVein AV400 infrared vein finder was used; it revealed one large vein with an extensive network of small superficial branching vessels localized to the area of the atrophic plaque. A working diagnosis of probable RICH was made.

clinical_record:
A 65-year-old woman presented with blurry vision in her right eye for several months. Ocular history included 3 recurrent episodes of bilateral iritis occurring during 5 months, amblyopia in the left eye, and bilateral posterior chamber intraocular lens. Patient had undergone left-sided mastectomy 2.5 years prior and had been on anastrozole therapy for more than 2 years. Medical history and past medication use were otherwise unremarkable.

Visual acuity: 20/25 OD and 20/150 OS without improvement on pinhole testing. Intraocular pressures were normal. Right eye showed trace conjunctival injection without definite ciliary flush, 2+ fine keratic precipitates, and 1+ cells in the anterior chamber. Left eye had a few keratic precipitates. Dilated fundus examination revealed cystoid macular edema with a yellow spot in the fovea in the right eye and an epiretinal membrane in the left eye. No inflammation in the periphery was noted in either eye.

reference_diagnosis: Anastrozole-associated uveitis with cystoid macular edema

clinical_record:
A 20-year-old man with no significant medical history presented for evaluation before orthognathic surgery. On oral examination, there was a 1.5-cm diameter, exophytic, smooth, regular, and soft lesion on the midline of the dorsal tongue. The patient reported that the lesion had been present since birth and had not changed in size or character. Vital signs were within normal limits. An MRI of the tongue showed a 1.5-cm protuberant mass arising from the dorsal aspect of the tongue in the midline at the junction of the oral component and base; the lesion appeared partly fatty, likely submucosal, demonstrated mild contrast enhancement, had intact overlying mucosa, and showed no involvement of intrinsic tongue muscles. The sublingual space and major salivary glands appeared normal.
